passage:
Good evening everyone, and welcome to Community Radio, broadcasting from the Jing'an district community centre. Today we have a very special announcement about this year's Winter Light Festival, happening on Saturday the 26th of December from 6 pm until 10 pm in People's Park, right here in Jing'an.
First, a word about how to get there. If you're taking the metro, please exit at Gate 3 of People's Square station and follow the blue lantern signs. For those driving, parking around the park will be extremely limited on the night, and the northern car park will close at 4 pm for event setup, so public transport is strongly recommended. There will also be extra bus runs: the 42 and the 109 will run every 8 minutes between 6 and 10:30 pm.
Now the programme highlights. At 6:30, the official opening ceremony will feature the district choir and the lighting of the main Christmas tree, which stands 18 metres tall this year. At 7:30, the drone light show begins — weather permitting — forming the characters for 'New Year's greetings' above the lake. At 8:30, the community seniors will perform a traditional lion dance near the main stage. And from 9 to 10 pm, there's a fireworks finale on the hour.
Food and drink: fourteen stalls will line the south promenade, offering roast chestnuts, hot wonton soup, baked sweet potatoes, mulled cider and festive pastries. All stalls are cashless this year — they accept mobile payment only — so please bring your phone or a payment card.
For families, the children's craft tent stays open until 9:30 pm, with free make-your-own lantern workshops. The library tent collects donated storybooks for the winter book donation drive — last year we gathered over 3,000 books for rural primary schools, and this year the organiser hopes to beat that number.
A few important notices. Entry is free, but the number of visitors is capped at around 8,000 for safety. Arrive before 7 pm for comfortable viewing. The lion-dance area will be cordoned off for 15 minutes after each performance. And please remember: do not touch or climb any light installations — they are works by local artists and quite fragile.
If you have any questions, call the community centre hotline on 12345-678 or check our official WeChat account, jing'ancommunity. The festival is organised by the district cultural bureau together with twelve local universities and more than forty volunteers. See you there, and happy holidays!
